title: How to Get a 7 in IB Biology: A Realistic Plan
summary: A realistic 12-week IB Biology study plan for a 7, covering assessment objectives, command terms, Paper 1, Paper 2, the IA, and weekly practice.
body_markdown:
Getting a 7 in IB Biology requires more than memorizing the syllabus. You need accurate recall, application in unfamiliar contexts, disciplined data analysis, precise responses to command terms, and a strong scientific investigation. The most reliable method is a repeated cycle of learning, retrieval, exam practice, correction, and retesting.


This **12-week IB Biology study plan** explains the current SL and HL assessment model, paper-specific techniques, weekly routines, and practical ways to measure whether you are approaching grade 7 performance.


### What does it take to get a 7 in IB Biology?


A grade 7 is awarded from your final weighted mark. Exact grade boundaries are set after each examination session and can change, so no permanent percentage guarantees a 7. Instead of revising toward an assumed boundary, aim to score consistently around **80% or higher** on challenging timed practice, which provides a buffer for examination pressure and boundary variation.


Under the course first assessed in 2025, SL and HL students complete two examination papers and one internally assessed scientific investigation. The official[IB Biology subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/recognition/pdfs/dp_sciences_biology_subject-brief_jan_2022_e.pdf) gives the following structure.


Assessment component SL duration HL duration Weighting


Paper 1A and Paper 1B 1 hour 30 minutes 2 hours 36%


Paper 2 1 hour 30 minutes 2 hours 30 minutes 44%


Scientific investigation 10 recommended hours 10 recommended hours 20%


**Paper 1A** contains multiple-choice questions. **Paper 1B** contains syllabus-related data-based questions, while **Paper 2** includes data-based, short-answer, and extended-response questions. The former Paper 3 and option topics are not part of the current model, as confirmed by the official[IB Biology curriculum update](https://www.ibo.org/university-admission/latest-curriculum-updates/biology-updates/) .


### Study around the IB Biology assessment objectives


Content knowledge is necessary but insufficient. Your preparation should address all four official assessment objectives.


Assessment objective What it requires How to train it


**AO1** Knowledge of terminology, facts, concepts, skills, and methods Closed-book recall, definitions, diagrams, sequencing, and flashcards


**AO2** Understanding and application of biological knowledge Topic questions, calculations, explanations, and unfamiliar contexts


**AO3** Analysis, evaluation, and synthesis of data, procedures, and predictions Graph interpretation, experimental evaluation, and extended responses


**AO4** Skills needed to conduct insightful and ethical investigations Planning, data processing, uncertainty, conclusions, and evaluation


Rereading may produce AO1 familiarity while leaving AO2 and AO3 weak. This explains why students can feel confident in class but lose marks when an examination introduces an unfamiliar organism, graph, or experiment.


Use[RevisionDojo IB Biology Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-biology-new/notes) to resolve specific gaps, then close the notes and retrieve the material independently. Every reading session should lead to questions.


### Master IB command terms


Command terms indicate the required type and depth of response. The IB's[assessment principles](https://ibo.org/contentassets/1cdf850e366447e99b5a862aab622883/assessment-principles-and-practices-2018-en.pdf) explain their relationship with assessment objectives.


Command term Required response


**State** Give a concise answer without explanation


**Outline** Summarize the main features


**Describe** Give a detailed account of a pattern, process, or observation


**Explain** Show how or why something occurs using causes or mechanisms


**Compare and contrast** Address both similarities and differences


**Analyse** Identify relevant parts, patterns, or relationships


**Evaluate** Weigh strengths and limitations before reaching a judgment


**Discuss** Present a balanced, evidence-based review


If asked to **describe** a graph, report trends, values, differences, and anomalies. If asked to **explain** it, connect those observations to biological causes. During practice, underline the command term and write distinct markworthy ideas rather than repeating one point in several forms.


### A realistic 12-week IB Biology study plan


As a starting recommendation, allocate **4-6 hours per week at SL** or **6-8 hours at HL** outside lessons. These are not IB requirements. Adjust them according to your starting grade, workload, and examination date.


### Weeks 1-2: Diagnose weaknesses


Complete a timed mixed assessment containing multiple-choice, data-based, short-answer, and extended-response questions. The[RevisionDojo IB Biology Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-biology-new/questionbank) can provide questions across the course themes.


Classify each lost mark:


- **Knowledge:** The relevant fact or process was missing.
- **Application:** You could not use known biology in context.
- **Data handling:** You misread a trend, scale, unit, or variable.
- **Command term:** The response had the wrong depth.
- **Precision:** Essential terminology was missing or vague.
- **Timing:** You knew the answer but did not complete it efficiently.


Create a red, amber, and green syllabus tracker. A topic is green only when you can answer questions about it under closed-book conditions.


### Weeks 3-6: Build knowledge and application


Cover two or three weak subtopics each week. Organize them through the current themes of **unity and diversity** , **form and function** , **interaction and interdependence** , and **continuity and change** .


Use this 60-minute block:


1. **10 minutes:** Recall the topic on a blank page.
2. **15 minutes:** Check and correct using concise notes.
3. **20 minutes:** Complete topic-specific questions.
4. **10 minutes:** Mark answers and classify errors.
5. **5 minutes:** Create retrieval prompts for mistakes.


Definitions, sequences, comparisons, and labels work well with[IB Biology Flashcards](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-biology-new/flashcards) . Flashcards cannot replace explanations or data analysis, however. After recalling a process, explain it in complete biological sentences and apply it to a question.


HL students should integrate additional higher level content into each topic rather than postponing it. Examination questions may connect SL foundations with HL mechanisms.


### Weeks 7-9: Shift to mixed examination practice


Reduce note-taking and increase mixed practice. A manageable weekly pattern is:


Session Main task Suggested time


1 Weak-topic recall and targeted questions 60 minutes


2 Timed Paper 1A set 35-50 minutes


3 Paper 1B data-based set and correction 60 minutes


4 Paper 2 short answers and extended response 75-90 minutes


5 Error-log retest 30-45 minutes


Mixed practice matters because the examination does not identify which chapter you need. It also reveals connections, such as how membrane structure affects transport or how selection changes allele frequencies.


Use[RevisionDojo's guide to Biology Paper 1 and Paper 2](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/comprehensive-guide-to-ib-biology-paper-1-and-paper-2) to review paper-specific expectations. Jojo AI can clarify a missing step, but rewrite the answer independently afterward.


### Weeks 10-11: Complete full timed papers


Complete at least one full Paper 1 and Paper 2 each week under strict conditions. Use the permitted calculator and data booklet, but remove notes and interruptions.


For every error, record the topic, assessment objective, reason for the lost mark, corrected principle, and a retest date within **2-4 days** . Award marks only when the required idea is clearly written. Mock Exams test overall performance, while targeted questions repair the weaknesses they expose.


### Week 12: Consolidate


Review your error log, essential diagrams, calculations, practical methods, and recurring command-term problems. Complete short timed sets early in the week, but avoid exhausting yourself with several full papers immediately before the examination. Reliable retrieval and sufficient sleep matter more than last-minute rereading.


### Paper 1 and Paper 2 strategies


For **Paper 1A** , answer every question because incorrect responses are not negatively marked. Eliminate options using biological reasoning, units, limiting cases, or contradictions. Move on when one item consumes excessive time and return later.


For **Paper 1B** , identify variables, units, scale, and uncertainty before interpreting results. Describe what the data show before explaining why, quote relevant values, and distinguish correlation from evidence of causation.


Paper 2 contributes **44%** of the final grade, so it should receive the largest share of examination practice. Keep short answers direct and terminology precise. For extended responses, briefly plan the concepts and sequence, then organize the answer around the question rather than reproducing everything you know.


Diagrams should be large, clearly labelled, and relevant. The official[IB Biology curriculum overview](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/curriculum/sciences/biology/) should remain your reference when checking whether content belongs to the current course.


### Train calculations, graphs, and scientific precision


Calculation questions often produce avoidable losses because students know the biology but omit working, mishandle units, or round too early. Practise writing the formula or mathematical relationship first, substituting values with units, completing the calculation, and giving a sensible final precision. Even when the final value is wrong, clear working may demonstrate valid intermediate reasoning.


Build familiarity with percentage change, ratios, magnification, scale bars, means, rates, and uncertainty where these arise in your course. Do not merely memorize a sequence of calculator buttons. Explain what the result means biologically and check whether its size is plausible before moving to the next question.


For every graph, check:


- The independent and dependent variables
- Axis labels, units, and scale intervals
- The overall trend and relevant comparisons
- Anomalies, overlap, or uncertainty information
- Whether the evidence shows correlation or supports causation


When drawing a graph, choose a scale that uses most of the available space, label both axes completely, plot points carefully, and use an appropriate line or curve. When describing data, support comparisons with values from the graph. A statement such as “group A increased more” is weaker than a quantified comparison using the relevant units.


Scientific vocabulary also affects marks. Terms such as **energy** , **concentration** , **gene** , **allele** , **diffusion** , and **active transport** are not interchangeable with casual alternatives. Train precision by comparing your response with the markscheme and identifying the smallest wording change that would make the biological relationship unambiguous.


When reviewing mistakes, separate mathematical errors from biological misunderstandings. A unit conversion problem needs short calculation drills, while a weak explanation of osmosis requires conceptual repair and application practice. This distinction prevents you from rereading an entire topic when the real weakness is narrower and more manageable.


### Protect the scientific investigation marks


The **scientific investigation contributes 20%** and has a maximum report length of **3,000 words** . A complicated topic does not automatically score highly. A focused research question, measurable variables, sufficient data, justified processing, and specific evaluation matter more than unusual equipment.


Your conclusion should answer the research question using processed data, address uncertainty, and compare results with accepted scientific understanding. Each evaluation point should connect a limitation to its likely effect and propose a feasible improvement.


RevisionDojo Coursework Review or IA Feedback can help check alignment with the criteria, but the investigation, analysis, decisions, and writing must remain your own.


### Measure progress and avoid common mistakes


Every two weeks, record Paper 1A accuracy, data-based marks, Paper 2 percentage, extended-response timing, repeated errors, and red, amber, or green topics. Several mixed papers at a similar level are stronger evidence of readiness than one unusually high score.


Common obstacles include passive rereading, revising only preferred topics, delaying data-based practice, ignoring command terms, failing to analyse errors, using obsolete Paper 3 resources, and neglecting the scientific investigation. Every content session should end with an independent attempt. If you cannot answer without support, the topic is not secure.


### Conclusion


Getting a 7 in IB Biology requires AO1 recall, AO2 application, AO3 analysis and evaluation, and AO4 investigation skills. Develop them through diagnosis, targeted study, mixed questions, timed papers, careful correction, and retesting.


The[RevisionDojo IB Biology resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-biology-new) can organize this work. Use Study Notes for defined gaps, Flashcards for retrieval, the Questionbank for application, Jojo AI for misconceptions, and Mock Exams for timed performance.
